merger_description:
All-Lora Pty Ltd (**All-Lora**), a wholly owned subsidiary of Adcome Pty Ltd (together with its subsidiaries, **Adcome**), proposes to acquire the business and assets of the IGA Allora supermarket (the **Target**) from Hymac Aisles Pty Ltd as trustee for the Hymac Aisles Unit Trust (the **Vendor**).

Adcome operates a network of 35 supermarkets predominantly across regional Queensland, including under the IGA, Cornetts and Everfresh banners. Adcome is owned and controlled by Gray Trading Pty Ltd. Metcash Limited also has a non‑controlling shareholding in Adcome.

The Target is an independently owned IGA supermarket at 41-43 Warwick Street, Allora, a rural township in the Southern Downs Region of Queensland, approximately 25 kilometres north of Warwick and 60 kilometres south of Toowoomba. It is the only supermarket in the Allora township.

The acquisition will occur by way of an asset purchase. All-Lora will acquire the goodwill, plant and equipment, stock and other assets of the business and take an assignment of the existing lease of the supermarket premises. Following completion, All-Lora will continue to operate the store as an IGA supermarket. Adcome does not operate any supermarket in Allora or in the nearby towns of Clifton or Warwick.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal overlap
between Adcome and IGA Allora in the local area surrounding IGA
Allora.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
